title_original: Gen Z investiert am meisten in Kunst – zumindest auf dem Papier
editorial_title_zh: Z世代在艺术上投资最多——至少在纸面上是这样

article_text:
Laut dem neuen UBS-Sammelreport gibt die Generation Z mehr für Kunst aus als jede andere Altersgruppe. Doch die Zahlen erzählen vor allem von den Superreichen – und wenig vom Rest des Kunstmarkts

Kunstsammler werden jünger und weiblicher. Das hat der "Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting" schon im letzten Jahr festgestellt. Nahezu revolutionär ist jedoch die neue Erkenntnis, dass die Gen Z jetzt die Macht übernommen haben soll. Diese Gruppe weist mit durchschnittlichen Ausgaben von 347460 US-Dollar die mit Abstand höchsten Investitionen in bildende Kunst auf – mehr als doppelt so viel wie jede andere Altersgruppe. Besonders bemerkenswert ist, dass die Gen Z für fast die Hälfte aller Käufe im Segment über einer Million US-Dollar verantwortlich ist.

Die Anzahl der Werke in diesem obersten Preissegment ist allerdings überschaubar. Die Mehrheit der Sammler bewegt sich weiterhin in niedrigeren Preisklassen: Über 80 Prozent gaben in der ersten Hälfte des Jahres 2026 weniger als 100000 US-Dollar aus.

Wie es zu diesen erstaunlichen Zahlen kommt, macht ein Blick auf die Methodik klar: Der Bericht, den Clare McAndrew ("Arts Economics") jeden Herbst im Wechsel mit dem im Frühjahr erscheinenden "Art Basel und UBS Art Market Report" erstellt, sieht diesem zwar zum Verwechseln ähnlich, basiert aber auf weniger überprüfbaren Daten.

Malerei bleibt das bevorzugte Medium

Der Bericht ist das Ergebnis einer Analyse von Selbstauskünften und -einschätzungen zu Ausgabeverhalten und Vorlieben von 3100 vermögenden Privatpersonen aus zehn globalen Märkten. High-Net-Worth Individuals (HNWIs) sind Menschen mit einem Vermögen von mindestens einer Million US-Dollar (abzüglich Erstwohnsitz). Die Untersuchung, die Mitte 2026 durchgeführt wurde, beschreibt einen Kunstmarkt, der einerseits durch eine starke Dynamik jüngerer Generationen und technologischer Neuerungen geprägt ist, andererseits aber in seinen Grundfesten traditionelle Strukturen beibehält.

Technologisch vollzieht sich ein deutlicher Wandel hin zur künstlichen Intelligenz. Während klassische Kunstpresse und Online-Plattformen die primären Informationsquellen bleiben, stieg die Nutzung von KI-Tools und Apps zur Kaufberatung sprunghaft an. Im Jahr 2024 nutzten lediglich vier Prozent der Sammler solche Tools, bis 2026 waren es bereits 22 Prozent. Die Mehrheit der Befragten bewertet die Auswirkungen der KI positiv, insbesondere im Hinblick auf die Auffindbarkeit von Künstlern. Sorgen bereiten jedoch Themen wie Marktmanipulation, Fälschungen und Betrug – Themen, die den Kunstmarkt schon lange begleiten.

Wie schon in den Vorjahren bestätigt sich, dass Frauen tendenziell offener und breitgefächerter sammeln. Sie investieren stärker in junge und aufstrebende Künstler sowie in digitale Kunst und besuchen im Durchschnitt signifikant mehr Kunstveranstaltungen als Männer. Männer hingegen konzentrieren ihre Ausgaben stärker auf etablierte Künstler und höhere Preisklassen. Trotz dieser Unterschiede bleibt die Malerei für beide Geschlechter das bevorzugte Medium.

Händler und Messen weiterhin die wichtigsten Vertriebskanäle

Ein überraschender Aspekt ist das gestiegene Bedürfnis nach Privatsphäre, das paradoxerweise am stärksten bei der Generation Z ausgeprägt ist. Diese Gruppe präsentiert ihre Sammlungen deutlich seltener öffentlich oder online als ältere Generationen . Regionale Unterschiede verstärken diesen Trend: Während Sammler in Hongkong die höchste Diskretion wahren, zeigen sich US-amerikanische Sammler am offensten und streben eher nach öffentlicher Anerkennung, beispielsweise bei Leihgaben an Museen.

Der Weg in das Sammeln beginnt für die meisten mit traditionellen Medien, wobei Malerei und Skulptur die häufigsten Einstiegspunkte bilden. Der stärkste soziale Einflussfaktor ist die Familie, was besonders bei der Gen Z deutlich wird. Interessanterweise gibt es kaum Belege dafür, dass der Kauf von allgemeinen Luxusgütern als Brücke zum Sammeln bildender Kunst dient.

Kunsthändler und Messen sind weiterhin die wichtigsten Vertriebskanäle. Gleichzeitig gewinnt der Direktverkauf durch Künstler massiv an Bedeutung. Der Anteil der Sammler, die direkt beim Künstler kaufen – sei es im Atelier, über Art Consultants oder über soziale Medien wie Instagram – hat sich im Vergleich zu 2024 mehr als verdoppelt und stellt mittlerweile den zweitwichtigsten Erwerbskanal dar.

Fokus allein aufs Topsegment des Kunstmarkts

Wer bis hierhin durchgehalten hat, gehört wahrscheinlich entweder zur Gruppe der HNWIs – oder hat Fragen. Mit dem, was in der Galerie in Düsseldorf-Flingern oder im Offraum in Berlin-Moabit verhandelt wird, hat der Report wenig zu tun. Am besten verdeutlicht das vielleicht ein Satz der Autorin Clare McAndrew, der man mit Sicherheit keine sozialistischen Anwandlungen unterstellen muss: "Zwar wirkt sich eine größere Vermögensungleichheit zweifellos nachteilig auf das langfristige Wachstum und die wirtschaftliche Stabilität aus, doch kann sie oft zu einer stärkeren Kaufnachfrage auf den Luxusmärkten führen."

Das Topsegment des Kunstmarkts muss sich seine Käuferschaft mit Luxusautos und anderen "Collectibles" von Uhren über Schmuck bis hin zu Handtaschen und Sneakern teilen. Für das Fußvolk des Kunstmarkts, das zur Vernissage nicht mit dem Chauffeur, sondern mit der U-Bahn anreist, fehlen vergleichbare Untersuchungen. Da wäre als Sponsor vielleicht nicht die UBS, sondern die Sparkasse gefragt.

title_original: Basquiat’s Long-Unseen Riff on Leonardo da Vinci to Lead Christie’s 21st Century Evening Sale with $30 M. Estimate
editorial_title_zh: 巴斯奎特长期未公开的致敬达芬奇之作将领衔佳士得21世纪晚间拍卖，估价达3000万美元
editorial_excerpt_zh: 《无题（达芬奇及其五张怪诞头像）》将在11月19日纽约佳士得21世纪晚间拍卖中领衔登场，这是其20多年来首次公开亮相。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "长期未公开的让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特杰作的重新出现，是艺术市场偶尔会上演的奇迹。佳士得周二宣布，其中一件作品将亮相其今年秋季的21世纪晚间拍卖。", "links": [{"text": "Jean-Michel Basquiat", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/jean-michel-basquiat/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据公告显示，《无题（达芬奇及其五张怪诞头像）》出自一个“杰出”的欧洲私人收藏，它将在11月19日纽约佳士得21世纪晚间拍卖中领衔登场，这也是其20多年来首次公开亮相。其估价“在”3000万美元“左右”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅明亮的橙色画布尺寸为84英寸乘84英寸，呼应了莱昂纳多·达芬奇的怪诞头像——这是一系列创作于15世纪末至16世纪初的墨水草图。这些令人毛骨悚然的讽刺画既是对时事的评论，也是解剖学研究，它们与这位艺术家惯常的优雅形成了令人反感的对比。巴斯奎特被创作于1493年左右的《被吉普赛人戏弄的人》（原名《五张怪诞头像》）所吸引，这是一幅对1420年前后罗姆人抵达西欧所引发的社会动荡的讽刺描绘。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴斯奎特承袭了达芬奇的所有五张头像，以及这幅画作中不羁的边缘感。当达芬奇以轻描淡写的方式夸张了其主体的主题表情、却仍赋予其躯体时，巴斯奎特将其剥离至只剩下恶劣的本质：黏糊糊的咧嘴笑、类人猿般的鬼脸以及狂吠的嘴。在它们上方写着“Muy Fao”，这是对西班牙语“muy feo”（意为“非常丑”）的拼写错误。佳士得表示，右下角的一块粉红色补丁包含了“ALTER EGO”（另一个人格）字样，指的是他自己。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "佳士得战后及当代艺术部主管安娜·玛丽亚·塞利斯（Ana Maria Celis）在一份声明中表示：“很少有画作能如此直接地展现巴斯奎特与艺术史分量的搏斗。我们知道巴斯奎特从小就对达芬奇的素描着迷，而在《无题（达芬奇及其五张怪诞头像）》中，我们看到他在应对正统艺术中最具感染力的主题之一——怪诞的同时，对这位伟大的艺术大师进行了即兴创作。一如既往，巴斯奎特能够彻底重振这一主题，在1980年代纽约的双重性和过度现象中对其进行重新语境化。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特的一幅充满狂怒的1982年骷髅画《无题》于2017年在苏富比以1.105亿美元的价格售予日本亿万富翁前泽友作之前，他一直保持着美国艺术家作品拍卖最高价纪录。（安迪·沃霍尔在2022年夺回了这一头衔，当时他的1964年作品《枪击萨黛·布鲁·玛丽莲》在纽约佳士得以1.95亿美元的价格售出，含买方佣金。）", "links": [{"text": "most expensive work", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/list/art-news/market/jean-michel-basquiat-most-expensive-works-1234585981/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅1982年的《无题》拍前估价超过6000万美元，成交价几乎是该估价的两倍。《无题（达芬奇及其五张怪诞头像）》的拍卖估价为其的一半；拭目以待市场需求是否能将其价格推高至或超越该艺术家的纪录。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
The re-emergence of a long-unseen Jean-Michel Basquiat masterpiece is a miracle the art market occasionally performs. Christie’s announced Tuesday that one will appear at its 21st Century Evening Sale this fall.

Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) will make its first public appearance in more than two decades when it leads Christie’s 21st Century Evening Sale in New York on November 19, having surfaced from a “distinguished” private European collection. The estimate is “in the region of” $30 million, according to the announcement.

Measuring 84 inches by 84 inches, the bright orange canvas responds to Leonardo da Vinci’s grotesque heads, a series of ink sketches made between the late 15th and early 16th centuries. These ghoulish caricatures were as much commentary on current events as anatomical studies, and they form a repellent contrast to the artist’s customary grace. Basquiat was drawn to A Man Tricked by Gypsies (formerly Five Grotesque Heads ), c. 1493, a satirical depiction of the social unrest caused by the arrival of the Romani in Western Europe around 1420.

Basquiat carries over all five of Leonardo’s heads, along with the drawing’s irreverent edge. Where Leonardo exaggerated his subjects’ expressions with a light hand but still gave them bodies, Basquiat strips them down to their foul essence: a slimy grin, a simian grimace, and a howling mouth. Above them reads “Muy Fao,” a phonetic misspelling of the Spanish muy feo , or “very ugly.” A pink patch in the bottom-right corner contains the words “ALTER EGO,” referring to himself, Christie’s said.

“Few paintings show Basquiat so directly wrestling with the weight of art history,” Ana Maria Celis, Christie’s head of post-war and contemporary art, said in a statement. “We know Basquiat was enthralled with Leonardo’s sketches from a young age, and in Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) we see him improvising off the great Master while tackling one of the canon’s most affecting themes, The Grotesque. Characteristically, Basquiat is able to completely reinvigorate the theme, recontextualizing it among the duplicities and the excesses of 1980s New York.”

Jean-Michel Basquiat held the record for the most expensive work by an American artist ever sold at auction after Untitled , a furious 1982 skull painting, sold at Sotheby’s in 2017 to the Japanese billionaire Yusaku Maezawa for $110.5 million. (Andy Warhol reclaimed the title in 2022, when his 1964 Shot Sage Blue Marilyn sold at Christie’s in New York for $195 million, including the buyer’s premium.)

The 1982 Untitled carried a pre-sale estimate in excess of $60 million and sold for nearly double that. Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) comes up for sale at half that estimate; stay tuned to see whether demand can push its price to or beyond the artist’s record.

article_text:
Two hundred years, so what? An anniversary calls for a party, and Paris Photo hasn’t skimped on the candles. For its 29th edition, the fair gathers 246 exhibitors from 38 countries, including 199 galleries and 48 publishers, with 80 newcomers.

“Paris Photo will be the first international event to celebrate the Bicentenary of Photography,” announces Florence Bourgeois, its director. Anna Planas, its artistic director, adds: “This anniversary is not only an opportunity to look back on the history of photography, but also to consider its transformations.”

Right at the entrance, Thomas Ruff sets the tone. Five galleries (David Zwirner, Konrad Fischer, Mai 36, Lia Rumma, Sprüth Magers, no less) have joined forces to unroll 36 meters of hanging, more than forty years of work, from analog photography to digital simulation. Nebulae, portraits, newspapers, pixels. Anna Planas speaks of an installation conceived as an “open book.”

Visitors walk along it more like a station platform, wondering which train to catch. A figure of the Düsseldorf School, Thomas Ruff has the elegance never to choose: for him, a photograph is both a document and a well-mannered lie.

In the Nave

At the heart of the nave, the Main sector lines up 152 galleries, and the dealers in vintage images hold court. Hans P. Kraus Jr. brings out treasures signed by Louis Daguerre, William Henry Fox Talbot, Anna Atkins and Girault de Prangey, those early practitioners who invented everything without knowing it. Gilles Peyroulet, Bruno Tartarin, Lunn and Serge Plantureux complete the caravan of origins. As Florence Bourgeois points out, “collecting photography today can cover very different realities: a vintage print, a complete series, archives.”

Yet it is in the 44 solo shows that the fair reads best. Merry Alpern’s prying windows, “Dirty Windows,” at Miranda. Stanley Kubrick, a photographer before he was a filmmaker, in the 1950s, at Duncan Miller. Kati Horna at Proyectos Monclova. Clandestine encounters in Bogotá’s movie theaters, captured by Miguel Angel Rojas in the 1970s, at La Cometa.

Pierre Jahan, a make-do surrealist, at Jean-François Cazeau. Malick Sidibé, Bamako’s king of images, at Magnin-A. William Klein at M77, Martin Parr at Rocket (clowning around, as ever). And Isabelle le Minh at Christophe Gaillard, who ties film into knots the way others tie a pastry ribbon. Among the eleven duo shows, Jane Evelyn Atwood and Stéphane Duroy share the in camera booth, two gazes that have never looked away.

Further on, the Voices sector is entrusted to two guest curators, Zasha Colah and Francesco Zanot. “What interests us is what happens when someone brings a perspective different from ours,” explains Anna Planas. Their theme, “La disparition” (Disappearance), starts from a delightful paradox: photography, invented to keep a trace of what fades away, celebrates its two-hundredth birthday just as its own form is slipping away.

The curators have gathered images designed to deteriorate or self-destruct, and others that merge into painting or sculpture until they are barely discernible. The metaphor has its limits, and the curators know it. “Considering the genocidal logics at work,” they warn, “this sector focuses on the self-destruction of the image, the recording of its own death and phenomena of disappearance.” Ulay has his solo there, at Charim, a ghost among ghosts.

Next door, the Digital sector has a new captain. Marco De Mutiis, digital curator at Fotomuseum Winterthur, brings together 13 exhibitors around the digital transformations of the image. His observation fits in one sentence: “We no longer ‘see’ through the prism of optics alone.” Photoshop, selfies, facial recognition, the like economy: the eye has changed glasses. And it no longer looks alone: “Our vision is augmented, extended and challenged by machines,” Marco De Mutiis continues.

This year’s guest of honor, the Centre Pompidou, presents “Révéler” (Revealing), around a hundred works by some thirty artists, many of them recent acquisitions, arranged in four chapters: “Faire l’image” (Making the Image), “À l’infini” (To Infinity), “L’atelier” (The Studio) and “Identités” (Identities).

The Cnap, for its part, lines up five works from its collection under a darkroom title, “FIX/DEV.” Fixer, developer: the smell of the trays is never far away.

Upstairs

On the first floor, the Emergence sector brings together twenty monographic projects from nine countries. Here you meet a carpenter napping in his workshop, photographed by Ricardo Cases at Galeria Reus. There is also the destruction of southern Lebanon, rewritten in poetry and calligraphy by Randa Mirza at Tanit. And the bold colors of Marguerite Bornhauser, at Porte B., who turns a net curtain into a blaze and a mesh into snakeskin. The Maison Ruinart Prize goes to Philippe Jarrigeon, presented by Womanray. His series “Le Vrai du Faux” (The True and the False), made this summer in Champagne, casts the Faux de Verzy, those twisted beech trees, as fairy-tale characters. Champagne for the trees.

The Elles × Paris Photo trail, launched in 2018, is entrusted this year to Aldeide Delgado, founder of WOPHA, under the title “An Oceanic Beginning.” “The sea becomes the starting point for a reflection on how the history of photography can be told,” she explains. The figure speaks for itself: 38% women artists at the fair in 2026, compared with 20% in 2018.

Along the trail, Berenice Abbott at Lunn, Sarah Moon at Howard Greenberg, Susan Meiselas at Magnum. Ishiuchi Miyako at The Third Gallery Aya, Mari Katayama at Suzanne Tarasieve. And Aletheia Casey, at Damiani, whose Australian landscapes look as if they came out of an oven.

At Paris Photo, books naturally have their kingdom along the galleries: 48 publishers from 17 countries, from MACK to Atelier EXB, from Aperture to Chose Commune, and more than 400 signing sessions. One could spend whole days leafing through favorite titles. The Paris Photo–Aperture PhotoBook Awards will be announced on Friday, November 13, at 3 p.m.

On the talks side, the Conversations program gives the floor to Thomas Ruff, Thomas Demand and Zanele Muholi, in dialogue with Tina Campt. Robert Adams, for his part, is recounted by three friends, Sarah Greenough, Mitch Epstein and Jeffrey Fraenkel. Sofia Coppola talks with publisher Michael Mack about the influence of photobooks. Plenty worth listening to.

Finally, for the first time, the Prix Pictet enters the nave with Valérie Belin and Alfredo Jaar. Plastic still lifes, a Great Salt Lake drained of life: beauty in the service of an account of ruin.

Beyond the Walls

Paris Photo cannot sit still. A whole constellation of satellites orbits the Grand Palais, and to keep from getting lost, Myrtille Beauvert and Elsa Seignol, founders of the New York agency Signals, have designed a free guide that runs on a phone. A map dotted in navy blue, a personal agenda, a continuously updated listing, and even a filter to keep only one-day events, the ones gone by morning. A pocket compass for a week that has none.

A rundown of noteworthy events. On Wednesday, November 11, from 9:30 a.m., the symposium “Le temps des épreuves” (The Time of Prints), co-organized by the City of Paris department for the preservation of photographic heritage, devotes its final day to the challenges of conservation, at the Musée du quai Branly. At 2 p.m., galerie 24b. opens “P×3 Prix” and “State of the World.” At 7 p.m., the Maison Européenne de la Photographie looks behind the scenes of Irving Penn’s fashion photographs. That same evening, Kometa celebrates its third birthday at Le Consulat Voltaire, until midnight.

Thursday, November 12, is an obstacle course. At 5 p.m., Stephan Vanfleteren opens “Transcripts of a Sea” at Rabouan Moussion. At 6 p.m., Mark Steinmetz hangs “Heure de pointe” (Rush Hour) at Galerie Ithaque, while Rebecca Topakian presents “Concentric Circles” in RosAlma’s Camion-Galerie (a gallery on wheels, someone had to think of it). That same evening, Polka opens two exhibitions, Steve McCurry’s “Immersion” and the ruins of Yves Marchand and Romain Meffre. The Hôtel La Louisiane hosts the fifth edition of Room Service, “The Silent Watchers.”

At 7 p.m., the Fondation Henri Cartier-Bresson leafs through At Night Gardens Grow with Pia Paulina Guilmoth, nocturnal gardens with the moon as the only light. To close the day, at 8:30 p.m., Sofia Coppola is the guest of Chanel’s “7 à 9” at the Jeu de Paume.

On Friday the 13th, Polycopies, moored at Port de Solférino aboard the Concorde-Atlantique, hosts Anders Petersen in conversation with David Campany at 4 p.m. The Jeu de Paume schedules two performances, by Davide Sgambaro at 4 p.m. and by Jérôme Grivel at 6:45 p.m.

At 7 p.m., Steve McCurry returns to the MEP for a talk followed by a signing, while Irina Rozovsky discusses her work at Librairie sans titre. In Belleville, Floréal opens “Gangsta’s Paradise” from 6 to 10 p.m., and the Fotofilmic gallery celebrates the launch of JRNL magazine.

Saturday the 14th belongs to books. Le Bal holds its signings from noon to 5 p.m., and Magnum Gallery runs its Magnum Book Festival until 8:30 p.m.

At 3 p.m., Véronique Ellena presents “Mains d’œuvre” (Handiwork) at MAC Créteil. At 3:30 p.m., Maciej Markowicz opens “huit secondes” (eight seconds) at Galerie XII. At 6 p.m., “She Is the Story” takes its final bow at Alta Vista Arts.

On Sunday the 15th, there is still Adam Rouhana presenting his book at the Grand Palais at 4 p.m., before the nave empties out. And the program doesn’t stop there: the Signals guide lists more than a hundred events over the week. You’ve been warned: you’ll have to choose.

Paris Photo is on view November 12–15, 2026, at the Grand Palais in Paris. 1–8 p.m. (7 p.m. on Sunday), VIP access from 10:30 a.m. Weekday ticket €36, weekend €41, student €26. The Signals Paris Photo Week guide is free and accessible from any smartphone.
excerpt_original: For its 29th edition, Paris Photo settles under the glass roof of the Grand Palais from November 12 to 15, in step with the Bicentenary of Photography. 246 exhibitors, 38 countries, and around the fair, a whole week of openings, talks and signings spilling across Paris.…

"paragraph", "text": "马尔凯作为野兽派画家而闻名。本作是野兽派诞生之前的作品，但粗犷的笔触和色彩运用中已可见其萌芽。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/b9f0aa522cdc1bd2ef38c531a04d62b6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮埃尔·博纳尔《在船上，韦尔农》1912年 油彩、画布", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是纳比派画家博纳尔的作品。坐在船上的女性后来成为他的妻子，背景的绿色与帽子的橙色对比非常令人印象深刻。纳比派与其说再现现实风景本身，不如说更重视色面的和谐与装饰性，画家的感觉与内心反映于其中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "paragraph", "text": "ドイツ・ケルン市のヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館・コルブー財団が誇る約7万点のコレクションより厳選された印象派とその前後の絵画70点を紹介する展覧会、「ゴッホの跳ね橋と印象派の画家たち」が名古屋市美術館で開催されています。マネからコロー、モネ、ゴーガン、シニャック、マティスまで42名の作品を通してモダン・アートの本流をたどるものです。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cbf5b9f60da99bf791c0aa12a770f429-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "フィンセント・ファン・ゴッホ《跳ね橋》展示風景より", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "モネやルノワールに代表される印象派の作品は、19世紀後半のフランスで生まれ、単に有名であるというだけでなく、絵画表現に大きな変革をもたらしました。本展では1章から6章まで印象派を中心に時系列で作品が紹介され、印象派が生まれる前段階としてどんな動きがあったのか、そして印象派の影響を受けた画家たちがどのように絵画のスタイルを発展させていったのかをとても分かりやすくたどることができます。美術の教科書に登場するような巨匠たちの作品をまとめて見ることができるという意味でも、大変貴重な機会といえるでしょう。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/5e4896966c9944fcf00890f4502605bf-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出展作家は42名にのぼりますが、このようにそれぞれの作家について簡潔な説明がついているので、「この絵を描いたのははどんな人？」と悩まずに済みます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "印象派以前"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第1章「印象派まで」と第2章「バルビゾン派」では、サロンを中心としたアカデミズムが主流だったフランスの画壇で、社会の変化に合わせて生まれてきた新しい絵画の潮流を紹介しています。例えば、近代化するパリを生きる人びとやその生活をありのままに捉えようとして、時に物議を醸したマネ、戸外制作で見たままの自然を描こうとしたクールベやブータン、そしてパリ郊外の自然豊かなバルビゾン村に集まり、風景という新しいテーマに取り組んだコローなどのバルビゾン派の画家たちを通し、印象派へとつながる流れをたどります。（以下、紹介する作品はすべてヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館・コルブー財団蔵 Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud, Cologne）"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/1efad1b5aa917a846fa5b3fc11367269-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "エドゥアール・マネ《アスパラガスの束》1880年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本作はマネ後期の静物画として名作と言われています。この作品には面白いエピソードがありますが、それはぜひ会場で。なお、マネは印象派を含む次世代の画家たちと交流があったものの、サロンでの発表にこだわり、印象派展には参加しませんでした。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/7d6fddc4d5f4457e598413974089fe73-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ギュスターヴ・クールベ《シヨン城》1873年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "伝統的序列の転倒を志向するクールベは、サロンに対して反旗を翻しました。それだけでなく、パリ・コミューンに参加し、多額の罰金を課せられたことも。本作で取り上げられているシヨン城は、かつて牢獄として使われ政治犯も収容されていたといいます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/7adfed136bf50c6b1f5c23f5919c3a0a-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ナルシス・ディアズ・ド・ラ・ペーニャ《秋のフォンテーヌブローの森》制作年不詳 油彩、板", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ほぼ独学で絵を学んだナルシス・ディアズは、ルソーを慕ってバルビゾン村に近いフォンテーヌブローの森を訪れるようになり、 暗く陰影の濃い林を好んで描きました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/b12c8b7e401505670006e9aa6ee0e2d0-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "シャルル=フランソワ・ドービニー《花咲く果樹園》1870年頃 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "風景画家としての地位を確立したドービニーは、素早く躍動感のある筆致で印象派に影響を与えました。さらに、印象派の画家たちをサロンで擁護したり有力な画商に紹介するなど重要な役割も果たしました。ドービニーを敬愛していたゴッホは《ドービニーの庭》という作品を描いています。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "印象派の登場"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第3章で紹介するのが印象派です。彼らは単に戸外制作をするだけでなく、光の効果を表すため「分割主義」と呼ばれる独特の技法を生み出しました。これは伝統的な技法とは相容れない表現であったため酷評を受け、ネガティブな意味で「印象派」と呼ばれるようになりました。しかし、個人の主観でしかない一瞬の印象を筆跡もあらわに画面に残した印象派の作品は、伝統を超えた新しい自由な表現への扉を開いたのでした。"}, "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/184e1fbbe38c6fb97ef918a7cd7090a8-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "写真で紹介したのはモネとルノワールですが、他にもアルフレッド・シスレー、カミーユ・ピサロ、ギュスターヴ・カイユボットなど、印象派を代表する作家の作品が次々と現れる第3章は、大変見ごたえがあります。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第4章でいよいよゴッホの《跳ね橋》登場"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "印象派そのものは1880年前後に分岐しましたが、印象派の作品から影響を受けた世代の画家たちは、それぞれに絵画表現を追求しつつ豊かな個性を開花させました。第4章ではポスト印象派と呼ばれた画家の中で、セザンヌ、ゴーガン、そしてファン・ゴッホを紹介します。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/6d58f877a83b152a3c3b13756107b189-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "フィンセント・ファン・ゴッホ《跳ね橋》1888年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "清澄な色合いが目を引く《跳ね橋》は、ゴッホの画業がもっとも充実していたアルル時代の作品です。パリ時代に印象派の影響を受け、明るい色彩を取り入れるようになった後に制作されました。ゴッホはこの土地がとても気に入り、ゴーガンへの手紙で「この冬にパリからアルルへと向かう旅の途中で僕が抱いた感慨は、今でもはっきりと残っている。『まるで日本にいるようだ！』って、ひたすら外を眺めていた。子どもみたいかな?」と書き送ったほどでした。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/150959d4ab52349cdf0bcb83e72c980e.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "フィンセント・ファン・ゴッホ《ニューネンの農家》1885年 油彩、板にカンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "こちらはゴッホがまだオランダにいた頃の作品です。夕日を背景に農家が抑制的な色合いで描かれており、《跳ね橋》とは対照的です。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/f470ecac932000fe5a8dfd123084d891.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ポール・ゴーガン《ブルターニュの少年》1889年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "裸の少年が横たわる姿を描いたゴーガンの作品。はっきりした輪郭線や平面的な色使いなど、彼が提唱した総合主義の特色を見て取ることができます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cb79e4279c41f852ca70d64e3b88ed04.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ポール・セザンヌ《梨のある静物》1885年頃 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ずっしりとした梨の存在感が際立つセザンヌの作品です。セザンヌは印象派の画家たちと交流があり一緒に戸外制作もしましたが、やがて画面の堅牢な構成を基本理念とする独自の表現を探求するようになりました。彼の作品もまた後世に大きな影響を与えています。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "点描技法を極めた新印象派の画家たち"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1886年に開催された最後の印象派展では、すでにモネやルノワールは参加しておらず、その時中心になったのはスーラやシニャックなど点描技法を駆使した「新印象派」の画家たちでした。点描技法というのは、印象派の筆触分割をさらに理論的に追求し、小さな点を科学的根拠に基づいて画面に配置するもので、濁りのない明るいトーンが特徴です。この技法はのちに色や形などの絵画的要素の追求へとつながり、20世紀のモダン・アートへの足がかりとなりました。第5章「点描派」では、フランスのみならず近隣のベルギー出身で点描技法を取り入れた作家も含め、バラエティ豊かな点描画が紹介されています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/c1afbf4162ab12ae0b90d81b40760587.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ポール・シニャック《カポ・ディ・ノリ》1898年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "新印象派の中心的存在であるシニャックは、スーラとともに分割技法を理論的に追求して点描技法を確立しました。本作は地中海の町を訪れたシニャックがその魅力を点描技法で表現したものです。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2d2a7c4e661bd24089796172dcaa48fd.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アンリ・ル・シダネル《ヴェルサイユの薔薇のある家》1918年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "シダネルは庭仕事も好きで、自宅周辺を薔薇で飾りました。本作は点描技法で描かれていますが、全体的に柔らかいトーンでまとめられており、シニャックとは違う味わいがあります。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/9f9973d041118c94c9574c3408f5de11.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "テオ・ファン・レイセルベルヘ《グリ=ネ岬、或いは夏の霧》1900年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ベルギー出身のレイセルベルへは、新印象派の影響を受けて点描技法を取り入れただけでなく、その技法に様々な可能性を見出していたといいます。しかし現存するレイセルベルへの作品は少なく、詳細な制作手法についてはまだ解明されていないとのことです。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "そしてモダン・アートへ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最後の第6章では「20世紀の色彩画家」として色彩の解放を果たしたフォーヴィスム、画家の内面や精神性の表現を重視したナビ派が紹介されています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/63fc1d2c7057b98132e093c3b87e1a93.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アルベール・マルケ《パリ郊外》制作年不詳 油彩、厚紙", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "マルケはフォーヴィスムの作家として知られています。本作はフォーヴィスム誕生前の作品ですが、荒々しい筆致や色使いにその萌芽が見られます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/b9f0aa522cdc1bd2ef38c531a04d62b6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ピエール・ボナール《ボートにて、ヴェルノン》1912年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ナビ派の画家、ボナールの作品です。ボートに乗っているのは後に妻となる女性で、背景のグリーンと帽子のオレンジ色の対比がとても印象的です。ナビ派は現実の風景そのものを再現するというよりは色面の調和や装飾性を重視し、そこに画家の感覚や内面が反映されました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/e1421195c3a6118b5e4396eb2b9fafd2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "モーリス・ユトリロ《サーカス、或いはヴォージラールの祭り》1927年 油彩、カンヴァス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ユトリロは「エコール・ド・パリ」の画家のひとりで、アルコール依存症の治療として始めた絵画が評価されるようになったという経緯があります。パリの祭りの風景を題材にした本作ですが、賑やかさよりむしろ寂寥としたイメージが伝わり、風景を描きながらも、画家の内面が強く作品に表れているようです。この先、美術の世界ではさらに多様な表現様式が登場し、現代アートへとつながってゆくのです。(ライター・岩田なおみ)"}, ドイツ・ケルン市のヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館・コルブー財団が誇る約7万点のコレクションより厳選された印象派とその前後の絵画70点を紹介する展覧会、「ゴッホの跳ね橋と印象派の画家たち」が名古屋市美術館で開催されています。マネからコロー、モネ、ゴーガン、シニャック、マティスまで42名の作品を通してモダン・アートの本流をたどるものです。

モネやルノワールに代表される印象派の作品は、19世紀後半のフランスで生まれ、単に有名であるというだけでなく、絵画表現に大きな変革をもたらしました。本展では1章から6章まで印象派を中心に時系列で作品が紹介され、印象派が生まれる前段階としてどんな動きがあったのか、そして印象派の影響を受けた画家たちがどのように絵画のスタイルを発展させていったのかをとても分かりやすくたどることができます。美術の教科書に登場するような巨匠たちの作品をまとめて見ることができるという意味でも、大変貴重な機会といえるでしょう。

出展作家は42名にのぼりますが、このようにそれぞれの作家について簡潔な説明がついているので、「この絵を描いたのははどんな人？」と悩まずに済みます。

印象派以前

第1章「印象派まで」と第2章「バルビゾン派」では、サロンを中心としたアカデミズムが主流だったフランスの画壇で、社会の変化に合わせて生まれてきた新しい絵画の潮流を紹介しています。例えば、近代化するパリを生きる人びとやその生活をありのままに捉えようとして、時に物議を醸したマネ、戸外制作で見たままの自然を描こうとしたクールベやブータン、そしてパリ郊外の自然豊かなバルビゾン村に集まり、風景という新しいテーマに取り組んだコローなどのバルビゾン派の画家たちを通し、印象派へとつながる流れをたどります。（以下、紹介する作品はすべてヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館・コルブー財団蔵 Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud, Cologne）

本作はマネ後期の静物画として名作と言われています。この作品には面白いエピソードがありますが、それはぜひ会場で。なお、マネは印象派を含む次世代の画家たちと交流があったものの、サロンでの発表にこだわり、印象派展には参加しませんでした。

伝統的序列の転倒を志向するクールベは、サロンに対して反旗を翻しました。それだけでなく、パリ・コミューンに参加し、多額の罰金を課せられたことも。本作で取り上げられているシヨン城は、かつて牢獄として使われ政治犯も収容されていたといいます。

ほぼ独学で絵を学んだナルシス・ディアズは、ルソーを慕ってバルビゾン村に近いフォンテーヌブローの森を訪れるようになり、 暗く陰影の濃い林を好んで描きました。

風景画家としての地位を確立したドービニーは、素早く躍動感のある筆致で印象派に影響を与えました。さらに、印象派の画家たちをサロンで擁護したり有力な画商に紹介するなど重要な役割も果たしました。ドービニーを敬愛していたゴッホは《ドービニーの庭》という作品を描いています。

印象派の登場

第3章で紹介するのが印象派です。彼らは単に戸外制作をするだけでなく、光の効果を表すため「分割主義」と呼ばれる独特の技法を生み出しました。これは伝統的な技法とは相容れない表現であったため酷評を受け、ネガティブな意味で「印象派」と呼ばれるようになりました。しかし、個人の主観でしかない一瞬の印象を筆跡もあらわに画面に残した印象派の作品は、伝統を超えた新しい自由な表現への扉を開いたのでした。

写真で紹介したのはモネとルノワールですが、他にもアルフレッド・シスレー、カミーユ・ピサロ、ギュスターヴ・カイユボットなど、印象派を代表する作家の作品が次々と現れる第3章は、大変見ごたえがあります。

第4章でいよいよゴッホの《跳ね橋》登場

印象派そのものは1880年前後に分岐しましたが、印象派の作品から影響を受けた世代の画家たちは、それぞれに絵画表現を追求しつつ豊かな個性を開花させました。第4章ではポスト印象派と呼ばれた画家の中で、セザンヌ、ゴーガン、そしてファン・ゴッホを紹介します。

清澄な色合いが目を引く《跳ね橋》は、ゴッホの画業がもっとも充実していたアルル時代の作品です。パリ時代に印象派の影響を受け、明るい色彩を取り入れるようになった後に制作されました。ゴッホはこの土地がとても気に入り、ゴーガンへの手紙で「この冬にパリからアルルへと向かう旅の途中で僕が抱いた感慨は、今でもはっきりと残っている。『まるで日本にいるようだ！』って、ひたすら外を眺めていた。子どもみたいかな?」と書き送ったほどでした。

こちらはゴッホがまだオランダにいた頃の作品です。夕日を背景に農家が抑制的な色合いで描かれており、《跳ね橋》とは対照的です。

裸の少年が横たわる姿を描いたゴーガンの作品。はっきりした輪郭線や平面的な色使いなど、彼が提唱した総合主義の特色を見て取ることができます。

ずっしりとした梨の存在感が際立つセザンヌの作品です。セザンヌは印象派の画家たちと交流があり一緒に戸外制作もしましたが、やがて画面の堅牢な構成を基本理念とする独自の表現を探求するようになりました。彼の作品もまた後世に大きな影響を与えています。

点描技法を極めた新印象派の画家たち

1886年に開催された最後の印象派展では、すでにモネやルノワールは参加しておらず、その時中心になったのはスーラやシニャックなど点描技法を駆使した「新印象派」の画家たちでした。点描技法というのは、印象派の筆触分割をさらに理論的に追求し、小さな点を科学的根拠に基づいて画面に配置するもので、濁りのない明るいトーンが特徴です。この技法はのちに色や形などの絵画的要素の追求へとつながり、20世紀のモダン・アートへの足がかりとなりました。第5章「点描派」では、フランスのみならず近隣のベルギー出身で点描技法を取り入れた作家も含め、バラエティ豊かな点描画が紹介されています。

新印象派の中心的存在であるシニャックは、スーラとともに分割技法を理論的に追求して点描技法を確立しました。本作は地中海の町を訪れたシニャックがその魅力を点描技法で表現したものです。

シダネルは庭仕事も好きで、自宅周辺を薔薇で飾りました。本作は点描技法で描かれていますが、全体的に柔らかいトーンでまとめられており、シニャックとは違う味わいがあります。

ベルギー出身のレイセルベルへは、新印象派の影響を受けて点描技法を取り入れただけでなく、その技法に様々な可能性を見出していたといいます。しかし現存するレイセルベルへの作品は少なく、詳細な制作手法についてはまだ解明されていないとのことです。

そしてモダン・アートへ

最後の第6章では「20世紀の色彩画家」として色彩の解放を果たしたフォーヴィスム、画家の内面や精神性の表現を重視したナビ派が紹介されています。

マルケはフォーヴィスムの作家として知られています。本作はフォーヴィスム誕生前の作品ですが、荒々しい筆致や色使いにその萌芽が見られます。

ナビ派の画家、ボナールの作品です。ボートに乗っているのは後に妻となる女性で、背景のグリーンと帽子のオレンジ色の対比がとても印象的です。ナビ派は現実の風景そのものを再現するというよりは色面の調和や装飾性を重視し、そこに画家の感覚や内面が反映されました。

ユトリロは「エコール・ド・パリ」の画家のひとりで、アルコール依存症の治療として始めた絵画が評価されるようになったという経緯があります。パリの祭りの風景を題材にした本作ですが、賑やかさよりむしろ寂寥としたイメージが伝わり、風景を描きながらも、画家の内面が強く作品に表れているようです。この先、美術の世界ではさらに多様な表現様式が登場し、現代アートへとつながってゆくのです。(ライター・岩田なおみ)

ゴッホの跳ね橋と印象派の画家たち ヴァルラフ＝リヒャルツ美術館所蔵

excerpt_original: ドイツ・ケルン市のヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館・コルブー財団が誇る約7万点のコレクションより厳選された印象派とその前後の絵画70点を紹介する展覧会、「ゴッホの跳ね橋と印象派の画家たち」が名古屋市美術館で開催されています。
translated_title_zh: 【报告】戈霍的跳跃桥和印象派画家 瓦拉夫·里希尔茨艺术博物馆 ～在印象派中心向现代艺术的道路一望～在纳古屋市艺术博物馆到11月29日
translated_excerpt_zh: 由德国克隆的瓦拉夫·里希尔茨艺术博物馆·科尔布基金会赞扬的约7万个收藏品中精选的印象派和其后画70个点的展览“戈霍的跳跃桥和印象派画家”在纳古亚市艺术博物馆举行。

article_text:
Wildlife photographer of the year 2026 winners – in pictures

A selection of the winning images from this year’s competition across topics ranging from underwater to urban wildlife, and photojournalism to mammal behaviour. The overall winner is Federico Veronesi of Italy for his powerful image of an elephant carrying a dead calf

The winning photographs will be showcased at the Natural History Museum in London from 16 October 2026 until July 2027

Wed 14 Oct 2026 03.41 EDT

Wildlife photographer of the year 2026 | The Aftermath by Federico Veronesi, Italy | Winner, Behaviour: Mammals

Escape Artistry by Michał Michalski, Poland | Winner, Natural Artistry

The Great Divide by Alex Visbal, Colombia | Winner, Wetlands: The Bigger Picture

Shedding Light by Agorastos Papatsanis, Greece | Winner, Plants and Fungi

Night-Time Catch by Alex Lindbloom, US | Winner, Oceans: The Bigger Picture

bagan , or mobile net-fishing platform, in the inky waters off Papua. He started searching for sharks around dawn when the nets were still in the water. Initially lacking natural light for his drone’s camera, he found these sharks illuminated by the

bagan ’s bright lightsPhotograph: Alex Lindbloom/Wildlife photographer of the year 2026

A Watchful Eye by Aaron Sanders, UK | Winner, Animal Portraits

Shifting Sand by Sitaram Raul, India | Winner, Behaviour: Invertebrates

The Meeting Place by James Lewin, UK | Winner, Animals in their Environment

Afternoon Snack by Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas, Germany | Winner, Rising Star Award

Secret Worlds by Kutub Uddin, Bangladesh/UK | Winner, Portfolio Award

Cribraria aurantiaca is at a tiny and often overlooked stage in its life. Uddin became interested in slime moulds in 2024, and devotes much of his time to revealing this hidden world – exploring his local woodlands in West Sussex, where fallen logs and damp forest floors provide opportunities for discovering these fascinating organismsPhotograph: Kutub Uddin/Wildlife photographer of the year 2026

Warning Sign by Francisco Negroni, Chile | Winner, Photojournalism

Birdsong Painted in Light by Konrad Gräeter, Germany | Winner, 15-17 Years

Protective Pose by Anton Sorokin, US | Winner, Behaviour: Amphibians and Reptiles

Young wildlife photographer of the year 2026 | Labour of Love by Oscar Whitfield, Zimbabwe/UK | Winner, 11-14 Years

Making Morays by Tony Wu, USA/Japan | Winner, Under Water

Scenes from the Swamp by Isak Pretorius, South Africa Winner | Behaviour: Birds

Wily Coyotes of San Francisco by Loren Elliott, US | Winner, Photojournalist Story Award

Urban Jungle by Seth Forestson | UK Winner, Urban Wildlife

Flight of the Bumblebee by Amelie Davis, UK | Winner, 10 Years and Under

article_text:
Films and events

Dare

French Girls

Effortlessly moving from one moment to the next, Hyun Lee’s fashionably hip and charming micro-budget debut heralds an exciting directorial talent.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Hyun Lee

With Mia Kidis, Daia, Anya Beyersdorf

Australia 2026. 83min

Courtesy of Preliminary Materials Films Pty Ltd

Language English

Introduction

Mia is happily aimless, working odd jobs and hanging with friends. But when she’s scouted to become a model, new people and strange conundrums enter the frame. Showcasing an array of new talent, both in front of and behind the camera, Lee’s inventive exploration of the absurdity of 20-something life, unfolding against the backdrop of late-stage capitalism, is a welcome and unexpected breath of fresh cinematic air.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Atlantic Rhapsody

A young man embarks on a surreal quest to find his long-lost father in a remarkable feature debut that spans 20 years of recent Chinese history.

Filipiñana

This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.

The Fox

A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy.

article_text:
Netflix has unveiled the cast and a first image for Simon Verhoeven’s German-language romantic comedy Oktoberfest , set against the backdrop of the country’s world-famous beer festival in Munich.

Jeanne Goursaud (E xterritorial ) costars as an Oktoberfest waitress and single mother with a complicated personal life opposite Jannis Niewöhner ( 22 Bahnen) as a stressed businessman who gets stranded in Munich while on a business trip to the city.

When the two protagonists from completely different worlds are thrown together, they come to realize that they who have more in common than they initially realized.

Related Stories

Entertainment Hits $332.5B To Become World's Second Most Valuable Sector As Netflix, YouTube & Spotify Fly - Interbrand Report

'Nobody Wants This' Has Netflix's Best Scripted Comedy Return Of The Year Despite 28% Audience Decline For Season 3 Debut

The movie is produced by Quirin Berg, Max Wiedemann, Kirstin Winkler at Munich-based production house Wiedemann & Berg Film, the award-winning Munich-based production house behind features The Lives of Others a nd Never Look Away as well shows Dark , 4 Blocks and Pagan Peak .

Watch on Deadline

The ensemble cast also features a host of German household names including Senta Berger, Michaela May, Eisi Gulp and Marlene Morreis as well as newcomer Bosse Hopperdietz, alongside Peter Gallagher ( The O.C.), Fisher Stevens ( Succession ) and Bart Edwards ( The Witcher ).

“Oktoberfest is a wonderful, crazy place. Nowhere else can you experience perhaps the most romantic kiss of your life while someone is throwing up two meters away,” said Verhoeven. “People let their guard down quickly here, and that leads to surprising, honest, human encounters.”

Production began on September 15, 2026 against the backdrop of the Oktoberfest, with the cast and crew shooting on location among thousands of festival visitors, inside the real beer tents, and across the festival grounds.

Filming is continuing at the Studio Penzing near Munich where the world of Oktoberfest has been elaborately recreated.

article_text:
France Télévisions film chief Manuel Alduy has warned that the far-right Rassemblement National’s plan to privatize public broadcasting would devastate French cinema, stripping it from one of its biggest financiers.

“There will be no more investment by public television in French feature films. And since there are not enough such films for free commercial television, there will be fewer French films produced and impoverished French films in financing,” said Alduy, who oversees cinema and international series at France Télévisions, in a message sent to Variety.

Zendaya Sets ‘Dune 3’ Oscar Campaign for Best Actress in Category Shake-Up (EXCLUSIVE)

India’s Oscar Entry 'Gondhal' Unveils Global Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)

His comments come as the Rassemblement National (RN), led by Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella, is leading polls in the run up to the 2027 presidential election (the first round of which will take place on April 18).

Like any far-right party, the Rassemblement National represents a major threat to the cultural sector. But in France, that threat is even more potent because the country’s vibrant film community relies significantly on investments from broadcasters, as well as subsidies distributed by the National Film Board (CNC) to finance films.

In its latest budget proposal, unveiled earlier this month, the party outlined plans to dismantle the National Film Board, privatize public broadcasting and slash public broadcasting funding by €3.5 billion ($3.9 billion) by 2028, a cut of more than 90%, while keeping a handful of outlets, including Arte and Franceinfo, in public hands.

France Télévisions is one of the pillars of France’s film financing system, investing more than €60 million ($67 million) annually in the pre-financing of over 60 films, nearly a third of which are first or second features. Many of these movies would struggle to attract financing from commercial broadcasters, such as TF1 or M6, or even streamers, whose investments tend to be concentrated on more mainstream fare.

It’s not just French cinema that would be impacted by the loss of public television’s support. International independent cinema would also feel the blow. At Cannes this year, 81% of the movies that world premiered in the official selection were financed by France. More specifically, France Televisions co-financed seven films out of the 22-title competition. Besides French-language movies like Jeanne Herry ‘s “Another Day” starring Adèle Exarchopoulos, it backed films such as Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” Ryūsuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden” and James Gray’s “Paper Tiger.” The CNC, meanwhile, backed 69 movies playing in the official selection. The CNC resources don’t come from taxpayers, but rather from a levy on all theatrical admissions (including Hollywood blockbusters) that are injected back into the industry — a rare, virtuous model that is envied by many film communities around the world.

France Televisions is already facing a €47 million cut ($52 million) in funding for 2027 as part of its Finance Law (setting the national government’s budget), and a further €47 million ($52 million) cut in subsidies; while lawmakers are considering plans to divert some of the CNC’s resources into state coffers.

More than 170 filmmakers, including Palme d’Or winners Jacques Audiard, Justine Triet and the Dardenne brothers, alongside Costa-Gavras, Michel Hazanavicius, Julia Ducournau, Claire Denis, Mati Diop and Agnès Jaoui, have signed an open letter published in Le Monde on Wednesday warning that the cuts could lead to 400 fewer French films being produced over five years. They also called for a new cinema law to protect the financing system and adapt it to the streaming era.

“At a time when cultural sovereignty is unanimously celebrated in public discourse, the new budget bill risks causing an unprecedented disappearance of French cinema from our screens,” the letter reads. “Fighting to preserve the work of the CNC, to restore funding for public broadcasting, or to maintain a reduced value-added tax (VAT) rate for all cultural industries means defending a system and a principle that have helped sustain a vibrant and dynamic culture in France for years.”

The letter alludes to the fact that Canal+, France’s biggest private financier of cinema, has threatened to walk away from its €1 billion ($1.1 billion) investment agreement with the French film industry if the government goes ahead with plans to double the VAT rate on pay-TV subscriptions from 10% to 20%.

The proposed tax hike, included in the government’s draft 2027 finance bill, would cost Canal+ approximately €200 million ($224 million) annually, according to chairman Maxime Saada.

Speaking on French radio RTL earlier this month, Saada said the measure would effectively void the company’s five-year agreement with French film organizations, signed in July, which commits Canal+ to invest nearly €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in French and European films between 2028 and 2032.

In their open letter, the filmmakers estimated that the collapse of Canal+’s agreement alone would result in a €750 million ($841 million) shortfall for French cinema over five years.

These threats come as Netflix, which became France’s largest private contributor to local production for the first time in 2025, is calling for a cap on investments .

Last year, the streamer invested €308 million ($345 million) in audiovisual production and cinema; and while France Télévisions remains the biggest overall backer, with €476 million ($533 million) invested across film and TV in 2025, Netflix could overtake the public broadcaster by 2030.

On the TV side, the broadcaster has been increasingly forced to partner with streamers to finance ambitious television series, but such collaborations wouldn’t work on theatrical movies due to the country’s windowing rules.

The French film community is also concerned by streamers’ rising dominance over local content production.

“Streaming platforms, mainly American, are imposing an unprecedented standardization of content. Weakening our cinema means impoverishing our French and European identity,” the open letter says.

article_text:
NYC Weekend Watch is our weekly round-up of repertory offerings.

BAM A series on female possession begins while Ken Russell’s reconstructed The Devils continues—read (or listen to) our interview with Mark Kermode on it.

Roxy Cinema A print of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre plays on Friday and Saturday, the latter day bringing Silent Night, Deadly Night 5 on 35mm and Suspiria ; Halloween shows on Friday and Saturday while Ganja & Hess screens on Sunday.

Museum of Modern Art A Sergei Loznitsa retrospective continues while Sundays with Steven starts with 2005’s War of the Worlds and 1953’s on 35mm.

Film Forum A 4K restoration of Alexander Payne’s Citizen Ruth begins playing; Coco shows on Sunday.

Anthology Film Archives A Troma series continues while films by Frampton, Franju, Jean Genet, and Ernie Gehr show in Essential Cinema .

Museum of the Moving Image The international version of The Shining makes its U.S. premiere on Sunday, followed by the theatrical cut ; Goodbye, Dragon Inn shows on Friday; The Exorcist and a print of Poltergeist are featured in Handcrafted Horror .

IFC Center Ken Russell’s reconstructed The Devils continues on a restored 35mm print—read (or listen to) our interview with Mark Kermode on it—while The Exorcist , Grey Gardens , and Ju-On: The Grudge play late.

Nitehawk Prospect Park Godzilla and Halloween screen early on Saturday and Sunday.

Metrograph Bram Stoker’s Dracula , Beetlejuice , Peppermint Frappé , Cría Cuervos , Horror of Dracula , The Brides of Dracula , News from Home , The Addams Family , Something Special , Midnight in Paris , All That Heaven Allows , and Far from Heaven show on 35mm; Terence Fisher , The Leaves are Falling , Trains: Local Routes , and Darius Khondji continue.

"text": "音乐的选择本身也是对科恩兄弟邪典喜剧《谋杀绿脚趾》的一种致意，片中约翰·特托罗饰演了张扬的保龄球手耶稣·金塔纳。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Variety 热门文章", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“他们没有给我任何理由去拍这部电影。他们只是在大笑，”他说。“我想，‘我不知道这段经历会是什么样，但我知道它绝不会有压力。所以好吧，我们他妈的拍吧。’”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴登还拿他角色的标志性发型开起了玩笑，那是科恩兄弟从一张1960年代的照片中发现的。“我当时单身——那是2006年——我说：‘我要一直单身到杀青那天。’”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "伊桑则讲了另一个关于巴登对角色投入的故事。他回忆说，这位演员认为他的角色需要脸色苍白，因此在大部分的户外拍摄期间，一名年轻的制作助理会举着一把浅蓝色的小阳伞陪伴在他头顶。“难怪我们会嘲笑他，”伊桑开玩笑道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这位演员的致辞随后变得更加深情，他回顾了与这对兄弟合作对他的意义。“他们给我的不仅是一部杰作，还有在个人与职业生涯中受用终身的馈赠，”巴登说。“他们让梦想成真了。在我断言这绝无可能发生十年后，它发生了。而且它比我所能想象的还要好。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当晚还安排了音乐致辞，法国创作歌手贝纳巴尔（Bénabar）演唱了查尔斯·阿兹纳夫尔（Charles Aznavour）的《因为你相信》（“Parce que tu crois”），这是乔尔·科恩选出的最爱歌曲。五届格莱美奖得主安杰莉克·基德约（Angélique Kidjo）则演唱了雅克·布雷尔（Jacques Brel）的《不要离开我》（“Ne me quitte pas”），这是巴登的最爱之一。", "links": [{"text": "Joel Coen", "url": "https://variety.com/t/joel-coen/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影节总监蒂埃里·弗雷莫（Thierry "致辞还通过放映埃托雷·斯科拉（Ettore Scola）1997年的短片《1943-1997》契合了当下的时代主题，该片讲述了一个年轻犹太男孩在战时罗马逃离纳粹搜捕并在电影院找到避难所的故事。随着五十年意大利电影史在银幕上展开，男孩渐渐变老。影片在1997年以一个年轻的非洲男孩为逃避迫害而跑进同一家电影院结束，在过去与现在之间建立了呼应。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴登借用了这部电影的信息，强调了它在今天的现实意义。“从刚果到苏丹再到巴勒斯坦，‘绝不再发生’对所有人而言都意味着‘绝不再发生’，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔尔还向里昂的影迷群体以及电影节对共享电影体验的坚持致敬，赞扬那些依然热衷于“和许多其他人一起聚在一个黑暗的房间里、在银幕上观看电影”的观众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自1984年凭借新黑色惊悚片《血迷宫》开启长片导演生涯以来，乔尔·科恩与伊桑·科恩打造了美国电影中最具辨识度的电影谱系之一，涵盖了犯罪喜剧《抚养亚利桑那》、邪典至爱《谋杀绿脚趾》、大萧条时期的音乐漫游《逃狱三王》以及西部诗集式电影《巴斯特·斯克鲁格斯的歌谣》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
To the sound of the Gipsy Kings’ Spanish-language rendition of “Hotel California,” Joel and Ethan Coen took the stage at Lyon’s Lumière Film Festival on Friday evening to receive the Lumière Award, celebrating four decades of filmmaking with a characteristically irreverent tribute to the inventors of cinema.

“Thank you to the Lumières for inventing the movie camera, or we’d have been fucked,” joked Ethan, drawing laughs from the audience.

Related Stories

H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair

Ethan Klein Reacts to Hila Klein's Cheating Allegations Amid 'H3 Podcast' Fallout: 'Please Respect My Family's Privacy ... They Have Nothing to Do With This'

The musical choice itself was a nod to the Coens’ cult comedy “The Big Lebowski,” featuring John Turturro’s flamboyant bowler Jesus Quintana.

Popular on Variety

The star-studded gathering included Javier Bardem, Frances McDormand, former Lumière prize winner Wim Wenders, Robert Eggers, Michel Hazanavicius and Bérénice Bejo, Benoît Magimel, Antoine de Caunes and Caleb Deschanel, in town for a masterclass and the premiere of Laika’s upcoming stop-motion animated feature “Wildwood.”

Accepting the award, Joel reflected on four decades of filmmaking with his brother. “We did it because we love cinema and we love storytelling,” he said. “We’ve had, pretty much with certain exceptions, nothing but fun making these films over the decades.”

Bardem, who won an Oscar for his chilling portrayal of Anton Chigurh in “No Country for Old Men,” delivered one of the evening’s most colorful tributes, recalling how he initially tried to turn down the role despite being a longtime admirer of the Coens.

“I sat down with them in New York in their office and I was like, ‘Listen, I admire you, I worship you, you are amazing, but I hate violence, I don’t drive, and I can barely speak English. What the hell am I doing here?’” Bardem recalled.

“They gave me no reason whatsoever to do the movie. They were just laughing,” he said. “I thought, ‘I don’t know what this experience is going to be like, but I know it’s not going to be stressful. So yes, let’s fucking do it.’”

Bardem also joked about his character’s infamous haircut, which the Coens had spotted in a photograph from the 1960s. “I was single at the time – this is 2006 – and I said, ‘I’m gonna be single until the day I wrap.’”

Ethan had another story about Bardem’s commitment to the role. The actor had decided his character needed to be pale, he recalled, so during the largely outdoor shoot, a young production assistant would accompany him to the set holding a light blue parasol over his head. “And he wonders why we laughed at him,” Ethan joked.

The actor’s tribute took a more heartfelt turn as he reflected on what working with the brothers had meant to him. “What they gave me was one masterpiece and the gift of a lifetime, personally and professionally,” Bardem said. “They made a dream come true. Ten years after me saying that would never happen, it happened. And it was even better than I would have ever imagined.”

The evening also featured musical tributes, with French singer-songwriter Bénabar performing Charles Aznavour’s “Parce que tu crois,” chosen by Joel Coen as his favorite song. Five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo delivered a rendition of Jacques Brel’s “Ne me quitte pas,” one of Bardem’s favorites.

Festival director Thierry Frémaux drew laughs by projecting photographs of the Lumière and Coen brothers striking remarkably similar poses, before reminding the filmmakers that, in keeping with festival tradition, they would have to shoot their own version of the Lumières’ first film, “Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory,” on Saturday. After screening one of the original versions, he gave them until the next day to come up with their own take.

The tribute also struck a timely note with the screening of Ettore Scola’s 1997 short “1943-1997,” which follows a young Jewish boy fleeing a Nazi roundup in wartime Rome who finds refuge in a movie theater. As five decades of Italian cinema unfold on screen, the boy grows old. The film ends in 1997 with a young African boy fleeing persecution into the same theater, drawing a parallel between past and present.

Bardem picked up on the film’s message, stressing its relevance today. “Never again is never again for everybody, from Congo to Sudan to Palestine,” he said.

Joel also paid tribute to Lyon’s community of film lovers and the festival’s commitment to the shared experience of cinema, praising audiences who still relish “gathering in a dark room with lots of other people and seeing it on a big screen.”

Since making their feature debut with the neo-noir thriller “Blood Simple” in 1984, Joel and Ethan Coen have built one of American cinema’s most distinctive filmographies, spanning the crime comedy “Raising Arizona,” cult favorite “The Big Lebowski,” Depression-era musical odyssey “O Brother, Where Art Thou?” and Western anthology “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs.”

Their 2007 thriller “No Country for Old Men” won four Oscars, including best picture, best director, best adapted screenplay and best supporting actor for Bardem, while “Fargo” earned the brothers their first Oscar for original screenplay in 1997.

At Cannes, their remarkable run began in 1991 when “Barton Fink” swept the Palme d’Or, best director and best actor prize for John Turturro. They went on to win best director for “Fargo” in 1996 and “The Man Who Wasn’t There” in 2001, while “Inside Llewyn Davis” took the Grand Prix in 2013. In 2015, they returned to the Croisette as presidents of the festival’s jury.

Friday’s honor makes Joel and Ethan the second filmmaking duo to receive the Lumière Award, following Belgian brothers Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne in 2020. Previous recipients include Clint Eastwood, Quentin Tarantino, Pedro Almodóvar, Martin Scorsese, Catherine Deneuve, Wong Kar-wai, Jane Fonda, Francis Ford Coppola, Jane Campion, Tim Burton, Wim Wenders, Isabelle Huppert and Michael Mann.

The Lumière Film Festival wraps Sunday.

title_original: Walid Raad’s Way of Working Is Inspired by the Mirrors in Vampire Movies
editorial_title_zh: 瓦利德·拉阿德的工作方式灵感源自吸血鬼电影中的镜子
editorial_excerpt_zh: 他在威尼斯双年展及其他地方的作品将历史的缺失转化为艺术品。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "十几岁时，瓦利德·拉阿德（Walid Raad）经常拿着相机在故乡四处走动，只是为了试着去理解这个世界。乍一看，他当时拍下的黑白照片呈现出一种冷酷、抽离的视角。但他很快发现，对于满目疮痍的贝鲁特，理解终究是有限的。一天，路过一家面包店时，他拍下了橱窗里陈列的一个蛋糕。上面装饰着对一个名叫哈桑（Hassan）的人的生日祝福。直到后来在家里冲洗底片时——他的父亲把浴室改造成了暗室，并鼓励他的爱好——拉阿德才注意到上面的日期：这个蛋糕是为哈桑·纳斯拉尔拉（Hassan Nasrallah）准备的，他当时是黎巴嫩内战中崭露头角的民兵成员。拉阿德曾短暂地幻想过在里面下毒。“但我当时15岁，”他笑着对我说，“我是个胆小鬼。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "几十年后，拥有博士学位并在现代艺术博物馆（MoMA）举办过回顾展的拉阿德，在一系列数字制作的生日蛋糕中重新审视了那个形象，这些蛋糕是写给那些让人觉得难以庆祝的政治领导人的：祝阿里、卡迈尔、托尼、瓦利德生日快乐；祝亚瑟尔、埃利亚斯、纳比赫、阿明生日快乐。到那时，纳斯拉尔拉已成为真主党领导人；2024年，他在一次以色列空袭中身亡。拉阿德色彩斑斓的蛋糕既欢快又冰冷——这是他标志性的、将虚构与现实结合的悲喜剧风格。在他的蛋糕中，正如他的许多作品一样，宏大的政治事件在一个亲密的、人类的尺度上展开。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从某种意义上说，蛋糕项目始于拉阿德15岁的时候，它具备了他所有的标志性特征：他从一个真实的事物——一份文献——开始，然后推演其逻辑，创造出某种虚构的东西，甚至可能带有一点奇幻色彩。这种方法支撑了他的职业生涯，跨越了近40年且仍在继续。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WR-123-PRT_composite.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "Walid Raad/The Atlas Group: Festival of Gratitude , 2003/2021. Courtesy Paula Cooper Gallery, New York/©Walid Raad; Opposite: Photo Steven Probert Studio/Courtesy Paula Cooper Gallery, New York/©Walid Raad", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他的作品是今年威尼斯双年展主展中的亮点：当你读到墙上的文字说明，得知这些看似平淡无奇的床铺是由亚瑟尔·阿拉法特（Yasser Arafat）睡过时，他那些关于床、素描和照片的画作便生动了起来，文字称“据说他从未连续两晚睡在同一张床上”。这位巴解组织领导人经历过40多次暗杀，“他不敢掉以轻心……所以他过着——也睡在——流亡和移动之中”。拉阿德补充说，他花了30年时间寻找阿拉法特睡过的床，绘制着那些他似乎怎么也画不完的床垫和羽绒被。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "无论是床还是蛋糕，故事都直观地沿着图像的边缘展开：画中的床尚未完成，边缘贴着胶带，布满笔触。生日蛋糕则仿佛与成堆的照片一起从牛皮纸信封中被抽出来，就像是在法庭审判中作为证据提交。拉阿德说，他正在“创造我希望本已存在的文献”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/012_Tunis.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "Walid Raad: Far from quieting_Tunis , 1969–2026. Courtesy Paula Cooper Gallery, New York/©Walid Raad", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "学者赛迪亚·哈特曼（Saidiya Hartman）在双年展中特别指出了拉阿德的阿拉法特照片，她将他对“想象与思辨的信仰”描述为“至关重要的”。哈特曼毕生致力于想象那些在档案中留下有限痕迹的被压迫者的生活——那些被剥夺声音的人或文盲，那些声音仅在胁迫条件下被记录的人，或者那些必然过着地下生活的人——比如阿拉法特。她将自己的方法称为“关键虚构”（critical fabulation）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，拉阿德最著名的正是他将故事与图片、想象与历史结合的虚构方法。这种工作方式与他的核心主题密切相关：阿拉伯世界及其政治与冲突——尤其是拉阿德在青年时期经历的黎巴嫩内战（1975—90年）。虽然海量的图像及其相互竞争的叙事几乎定义了数字时代，但这个充满虚假信息的战场在该地区产生了显著的影响。“在战争期间，”今年在威尼斯双年展参展的另一位黎巴嫩艺术家哈利勒·若赖日（Khalil Joreige）回忆道，“每个民兵都有自己的媒体站、电视台、报纸或广播。这里存在着一场真正的图像之战”——若赖日称这场战争影响了他那一代人“与图像复杂的关系”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，哈佛大学艺术史学家卡丽·兰伯特-贝蒂（Carrie Lambert-Beatty）将拉阿德的作品描述为“准虚构”（parafiction）的典范，并补充说，艺术所能做到的最有力量的事情之一，就是让观众体验到某个特定场景曾经是真实的——并提醒他们其他世界是可能的。在其近期关于艺术研究的著作中，艺术史学家克莱尔·毕设（Claire Bishop）也单独提到了拉阿德，她指出，虽然该流派的许多作品都在重现信息过载的体验——比如展柜中的文献——但拉阿德以叙事的形式提供了综合，且没有落入那些基于研究的艺术所强烈反对的权威宏大叙事的俗套之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在我自己的书《寓言与取证》（Fables & Forensics）中，我将拉阿德的作品描述为信息时代的一种超现实主义，并指出他是如何以一种戏谑的形式来呈现普通却令人眼花缭乱的虚假信息过剩——但同时补充说，他从未落入复制假新闻的陷阱。任何可能被误认为真实的客观事实——一张床或一个生日蛋糕——都无足轻重，而且总有线索暗示其文献的人为建造性；只需记住去看看边缘。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MZO-Walid-Raad_9529_WEB.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "View of Raad’s installation Postscript to the Arabic Edition , 1938–2025, in the 61st Venice Biennale. Photos Marco Zorzanello/Courtesy Venice Biennale", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "瓦利德·拉德最为人熟知的作品是他作为一个名为“阿特拉斯集团”（the Atlas Group）的虚构集体所创作的，这些作品对摄影与真相之间紧张的关系发出了诘问。该集团的录像作品《人质：巴沙尔录像带》（#17与#31）（Hostage: The Bachar tapes (#17 and #31)）署年2000年，其中苏海尔·巴沙尔（Souheil {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉德说，该集团成立于1989年，解散于2004年。但日期和所有事实一样，都是他的媒介。你还会发现一些杂志和博物馆将该集团的起源追溯到1967年（拉德出生的年份）、1948年或1945年。并且，该集团曾将一些档案影像归属于并不存在的机构——例如纽约美术馆（Museum of Fine Art New Engines”）的版本，但各自列出的创作时间却不同（分别为2000—03年和1996—2004年）。尽管拉德表示他在2004年终止了“阿特拉斯集团”，但2026年威尼斯双年展的目录中却收录了一件该集团的作品，标注日期为“2023年印刷”——这使得它究竟是什么时候制作的、该集团是否真的已经解散，变得扑朔迷离。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WR-16-PH.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "瓦利德·拉德 / 阿特拉斯集团：《说实话，天气挺帮忙的_沙特阿拉伯》（Let’s be honest, the weather helped_Saudi "不过，有一个日期是明确的：在过去的2个十年里——自从2005年的一次转折点以来——拉德的作品变得愈发诡异。“阿特拉斯集团”曾引导观众以不稳定的眼光看待他的档案文献，但后来的作品则要求观众去面对缩小的物件、复活的画作，以及潜伏在档案中的吸血鬼。某种转变已经发生，而过去关于事实与虚构的陈旧语言仅触及了皮毛。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在纽约州北部所谓的“爱尔兰阿尔卑斯山”（Irish Alps）的一座山顶上，有一座修缮一空的19世纪谷仓，拉德在那里保存着一个一丝不苟的档案馆。距离他任教的巴德学院（Bard College）大约有1小时车程，他和妻子复制了这座谷仓的平面图，在附近建造了第二栋建筑：他们的家。从他们的门廊望出去的景色宛如一幅哈德逊河画派（Hudson River School）的油画，而初次见他感觉就像是拉开了帷幕的一角：20多年来，他一直勤勉地将自己的容貌从互联网的各个角落隐藏起来，用其他面孔充斥算法来扰乱追踪。他用一个词来解释自己的这种逃避行为——“恐惧症”（phobia）——但人们很难不把它看作是拉德运用摄影让世界变得更大、更陌生，而不是试图去“捕捉”它的另一种方式。见到真人时，他热情好客，并以“正确的方式”——配上漆树果粉和橄榄油——端上自制的塔布勒沙拉（tabbouleh）和鹰嘴豆泥（hummus）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这座谷仓里，拉德悉心整理了各种临时材料，例如他展览的墙面标签和参加晚宴的名片，所有这些都是未来可能会、也可能不会成为艺术品的素材。一个带带子的皮革作品文件夹里装着他早期的习作，包括他十几岁时拍摄的那些照片。他在波士顿上高中——“他们有暗室，还有篮球队，所以棒极了，”他说——在那里，他模仿辛迪·舍曼（Cindy Sherman）、黛安·阿勃丝（Diane Arbus）、加里·温诺格兰德（Garry Winogrand）、斯蒂芬·肖尔（Stephen Shore）、亨利·卡蒂埃-布列松（Henri Cartier-Bresson）和卢卡斯·萨马拉斯（Lucas Samaras）的风格拍摄照片。拉德能够模仿他们所有人的风格，但从这次练习中他最清晰地收获的，是从镜头背后具象化一种假面（persona）的体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WGR_2026_Portrait.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "瓦利德·拉德2026年自画像。鸣谢：纽约保拉·库珀画廊 / © 瓦利德·拉德", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1985年，拉德开始在罗切斯特理工学院（Rochester Institute of Technology）攻读本科学位，最初主修医学，随后转入摄影专业。在那里，他凭借化名P.X.切斯特菲尔德（P.X. Chesterfield）创作的一件作品赢得了他的第一个摄影奖，这个化名的灵感来自一位真实的美国海军陆战队将军P.X.凯利（P.X. Kelley），他觉得这个名字听起来很酷。不久之后，他入读罗切斯特大学（University of Rochester）的“文化与视觉研究”（Cultural and Visual Studies）博士项目，该项目拥有当时崭露头角的明星师资：克雷格·欧文斯（Craig Owens）、卡贾·西尔弗曼（Kaja Silverman）、道格拉斯·克里普（Douglas Crimp）。“那是精神分析、语言学和马克思主义，”拉德解释道，“神圣三位一体。”对拉德而言，假面、理论与摄影开始交汇融合。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为学生，拉德每年夏天都会访问并拍摄贝鲁特，这一习惯他延续至今。回到家乡后，他试图模仿他在父亲给他的摄影杂志上看到的黛安·阿勃丝或尤金·阿杰（Eugène Atget）的观察技巧。但他发现，“在一个到处都是狙击手的城市里……甚至像使用三脚架这样简单的事情都是不可能的。”他也并非在拍摄战地摄影，从不捕捉正在发生的行动，而总是记录事后的残局。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，在拍摄了爆炸后的遗迹照片后，拉德常常有一种缺失了什么的感觉，于是他开始亲自动手处理这些照片——用红铅笔将残骸圈起来。他最著名作品的萌芽在他十几岁时便已显露端倪，对于一个自称最初对“关于暴力和创伤的一种特定思考方式”感兴趣的艺术家来说，这似乎很贴切。那些红色圆圈的版本在阿特拉斯集团的作品《说实话，天气挺帮忙的》（Let’s Be Honest, the Weather Helped [1998/2006]）中再次出现，这是一组贝鲁特的黑白快照，上面标有色彩鲜艳的点，这些点对应的是弹药制造商用来识别弹壳和炮弹的代码系统——从而间接地识别出它们的制造者。在拉德手中，这些圆点与其说是法医式的记号，不如说更像是五彩纸屑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在“阿特拉斯集团”名下，拉德塑造了诸如赌博历史学家法德尔·法胡里博士（Dr. Fadl Fakhouri）和倒霉的警探尤塞夫·比塔尔（Yussef Bitar）等人物——他解释道，这是些“非常严肃、非常专业的人”——他们是那种很可能会留下官方文件的人。但最终，他发现“阿特拉斯集团”有“一定的局限性”，并开始对展现“暴力具有比我们所知更具潜伏性的影响”产生兴趣。此外，他补充道，到21世纪初，他觉得“地图和档案的语言已经精疲力竭了”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉德的想法开始转变，起因是在20世纪90年代初，他在参与一个关于黎巴嫩南部占领的录像项目时，遇到了黎巴嫩作家兼艺术家贾拉尔·图菲克（Jalal Toufic）。他开始阅读图菲克的书，起初觉得难以理解，但最终他读到了《即将来临》（Forthcoming (2000)）。该书收录了一个故事：一位受过古典训练的摄影师不断拍摄贝鲁特建筑的模糊照片。拉德瞬间认出了自己。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉德对我说：“我吓坏了。就好像他能听到我的内心独白一样。”他想到了在战时贝鲁特，某些摄影惯例——比如像三脚架这样简单的事物——是如何变得对他而言无法使用的，但不久之后，他开始更广泛地思考暴力从他身上剥夺走的一切。他在罗彻斯特接受的三位一体训练告诉他，“语言、心灵、经济……这些才是世界的素材”。他说，图菲克为他从未接触过的“另一个地方”赋予了语言。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自那次相遇以来，图菲克几乎影响了拉德创作的一切。“我为自己谈论那个家伙的次数之多感到不好意思，”他对我说，“就好像我没有一个思想不是经由他传递的。”具有持久影响的是图菲克的“退隐”（withdrawal）概念，这一概念在《超越毁灭的过去传统的退隐》（The Withdrawal of Tradition Past a Surpassing Disaster (2009)）中阐述得最为明确，在早期的文章中也有涉及。在书中，他描述了重大文化动荡之后可能出现的种种非物质损失——当孕育它们的社会被灾难不可逆转地改变时，仪式和形式如何变得不可用或失去效力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "图菲克理论认为，灾难过后，人们可能会坚定不移地执着于传统，就像犹太人大屠杀后正统犹太教的复兴那样；或者传统也可能被彻底压制，正如两次世界大战后，某些现代主义流派妄图构想一张白纸并废除前代传统一样。当传统在新的语境中复活时，总有哪里是不对劲的：图菲克将这种行为称作“复活”，因为传统与其说是活着的，不如说是僵尸般的。艺术家的任务就是让这种退隐变得切实可感——让缺席呈现出来，“就像吸血鬼电影里的镜子一样”；在图菲克看来，只有那些尝试复活退隐传统却失败了的人，“才能真正彻底地成为现代人”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种退隐的概念为拉德在阿拉伯世界首家白立方画廊——于2005年开幕的斯费尔-塞姆勒画廊（Sfeir-Semler Gallery）——展出的关键作品提供了灵感。他曾多次拒绝邀请，直到2008年才最终默许，因为他感觉有些不对劲。当他到达画廊时，他发现自己寄去的“阿特拉斯集团”的作品被缩小到了原本尺寸的1/100。当我向拉德追问这怎么可能时，他说“在某些情况下，你自己的作品不再为你所用，你与它的唯一关系也会变得扭曲”。对他而言，这既不是“一种症状，也不是隐喻”。它既“不是量子效应”，也不是“人的心理、物质条件或语言”的一种状况——他说，“这是‘退隐’”。退隐也是他无法完成那些阿拉法特床铺画作的根本原因。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉德与图菲克之间的相似性如此惊人，以至于不止一个人坦言怀疑图菲克其实只是拉德的另一个分身——如果这是真的，这一理论将需要一个精心策划的骗局，即拉德雇佣替身在公开活动中与他并肩出现。然而，尽管拉德无疑擅长构筑虚构和分身，但他对恶作剧的兴趣不及对寓言的兴趣——比起诡计与幻觉，他更关注当某事被想象为真实发生过时会发生什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/002_Hussein_20X15@300.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "由纽约保拉·库珀画廊提供 / ©Walid Raad", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在“阿特拉斯集团”对档案进行深挖并使其变得陌生之后，拉德的作品超越了对事实与虚构的打乱重组，走向了更接近魔幻现实主义的风格。在此过程中，那个很难让人不联想到真相的摄影媒介，其核心地位逐渐减弱。《最好一次又一次地看云》（Better be watching the clouds again and again (2000/2017)）是一系列拼贴作品，署名属于一位受过植物学家训练的虚构黎巴嫩陆军军官法德瓦·哈苏恩（Fadwa Hassoun）。战争期间，哈苏恩将花卉作为代号指派给政治人物，讲述她故事的作品中出现了本杰明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）、萨达姆·侯赛因（Saddam Hussein）、罗纳德·里根（Ronald Reagan）等人的黑白肖像，他们的头部顶着五颜六色的花瓣，双腿则被做成茎干的模样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "近期，拉阿德与平面设计师皮埃尔·于盖巴尔（Pierre Huyghebaert）合作创作了《我想我能逃脱命运（再次）》（2025），这是一件汇集了相关人士言论的装置作品，这些人因表达对巴勒斯坦的声援而被取消了展览和项目的资格。这些引文被印出、剪下并贴在画廊的踢脚线低处，如果不蹲下来很难看清。真正抓人眼球的是沿着墙壁延伸的彩色胶带条，它们就像是那些永远无法在这样空间里悬挂的艺术品的占位符。这又是一个灾难如何在艺术中侧面呈现的例子，印证了图菲克的观点：冲突留下的痕迹在艺术品和文化传统中仅以“缺席”的形式可见——一件“真正现代”的艺术品能够让这种缺席显形。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2025-mathaf-we-refuse-d-1251.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "瓦利德·拉阿德（与皮埃尔·于盖巴尔合作）：《我想我能逃脱命运（再次）》，2025年；展出于卡塔尔多哈阿拉伯现代美术馆（Mathaf）2025–26年展览“we refuse_d”中。图片由纽约保拉·库珀画廊及多哈阿拉伯现代美术馆提供/©Walid Raad", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "托菲克的吸罗（vampire-mirror）理念也再次出现在瓦利德·拉德在威尼斯展出的其他作品中，与阿拉法特的作品一同展出。被盗的阿拉伯和土耳其艺术品的复制品被绘制在木托盘的底部。在这里，正如他近来的几件作品一样，拉德这位吸血鬼举起镜子照向了现代阿拉伯艺术本身，该艺术最近经历了一个被艺术界最喜爱的词汇所形容的“重新发现”时期——或者说，是复活。当黎巴嫩内战于1990年结束时，一面墙上贴着的文字说明写道，民兵们出售了武器，其中许多武器流落到了巴尔干地区；因此，南斯拉夫内战部分是由黎巴嫩武器打响的。文字还补充说，这些彩绘托盘最近在卢布尔雅那的现代美术馆（Moderna Galerija）被发现——而就在不久前，他才刚刚在那里的举办了一场中期回顾展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "明年春天，在纽约的保拉·库珀画廊，拉阿德将在画廊里把一辆复古大众甲壳虫汽车像一只垂死的虫子一样背朝下放置——这是对“飞翔的大众汽车”的致敬，美国士兵正是这样称呼他们在1980年代向贝鲁特发射的火炮炮弹。环绕四周的墙上将是士兵们用英语、俄语、阿拉伯语、希伯来语和法语等各种语言留在炸弹上的手写字条复制品——比如“xoxo”、或者“因果的假阳具很少是带着润滑油到达的”（the dildo of consequences rarely arrives lubed）、或者“来自硅谷的爱”。拉阿德在 Reddit 上找到了世界各地那些爱吹嘘的士兵发布的图片，然后夸大了他们铭文的尺寸并改变了颜色。这件作品中并没有太多的虚构或幻想：有时，事实本身就足够离奇。", "translated": true}]

One day, walking by a bakery, he snapped a cake displayed in the window. It was decorated with birthday wishes for someone named Hassan. Only later, developing the film at home—his dad had converted the bathroom to a darkroom, encouraging his hobby—did Raad register the date: The cake was for Hassan Nasrallah, then a rising militiaman in the Lebanese Civil War. By then, Nasrallah had become the leader of Hezbollah; in 2024, he was killed in an Israeli airstrike. Raad’s colorful cakes are at once cheerful and cold—his trademark tragicomic blend of fiction and fact. In his cakes, as in so much of his work, grand political events unfold on an intimate, human scale."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Begun, in a sense, when Raad was just 15, the cake project has everything of his signature: He starts with something true—a document—then extrapolates its logic to create something fictional, maybe even a little fantastical.
